newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand ends firmer after becalmed session.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand ends firmer after becalmed session.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended firmer on exporter demand after a becalmed Thursday session as business thinned out due to holidays in the United States.
The currency spent most of the afternoon around US$0.7082-89 before closing at US$0.7082,89 and 66.79 on the Trade-Weighted Index, up from 0.7062/69 and 66.63 at the open.
There was a possibility of a shift lower if stop loss orders were triggered around the 0.7060 level, which may see a shift down to around US$0.6900, one Auckland dealer said.
"But I still view the Kiwi was being relatively underprinned with some good quality export buyers, so I can't see it drifting much below 70 U.S. cents," he said.
A continuation of tight range trade was expected overnight.
